title.raw: 卷一百七十七 列傳第六十四: 張思明 吳元珪 張昇 臧夢解 陳顥 Volume 177 Biographies 64: Zhang Siming, Wu Yuangui, Zhang Sheng, Zang Mengjie, Chen Hao

sentences.zh: 張思明

translations.literal: Zhang Siming
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming

sentences.zh: 張思明，字士瞻，其先獲嘉人，後​​徙居輝州。

translations.literal: Zhang Siming, courtesy name Shizhan, his ancestors were men of Huojia, and later moved to reside in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Siming, courtesy name Shizhan, came from a family originally of Huojia who later settled in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 思明穎悟過人，讀書日記千言。

translations.literal: Siming was quick-witted beyond others; in reading books he memorized a thousand words each day.
translations.idiomatic: Siming was exceptionally bright; he could memorize a thousand characters a day from his reading.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，由侍儀司舍人辟御史臺掾，又辟尚書省掾。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, through his post as Attendant of the Ceremonial Office he was recruited as a clerk of the Censorate, and again recruited as a clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Zhiyuan reign, while serving as an attendant in the Ceremonial Office, he was recruited first as a clerk in the Censorate and then in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 左丞相阿合馬既死，世祖追咎其奸欺，命尚書簿問遺孽。

translations.literal: After the Left Chancellor Ahmad died, Kublai pursued blame for his deceit and fraud and ordered the Ministry to register and interrogate his remaining associates.
translations.idiomatic: After Left Chancellor Ahmad's death, Kublai held him accountable for his fraud and ordered the Ministry of Works to investigate and question his remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 一日，召右丞何榮祖、左丞馬紹，盡輸其贓以入，思明抱牘從，日已昏，命讀之，自昏達曙，帝聽忘疲，曰：「讀人吐音，大似侍儀舍人。

translations.literal: One day, he summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to turn in all their illicit gains; Siming, holding documents, followed; the day had already grown dark, and the Emperor ordered them read; from dusk until dawn he listened without tiring and said: "The reader's enunciation greatly resembles that of a Ceremonial Office attendant.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor summoned Right Chancellor He Rongzu and Left Chancellor Ma Shao to surrender all their ill-gotten gains. Siming followed with the documents. Night had already fallen, but the Emperor ordered them read aloud; he listened from dusk until dawn without fatigue and said, "The reader's pronunciation sounds very much like a Ceremonial Office attendant.

sentences.zh: 」右丞對曰：「正由舍人選為掾。

translations.literal: " The right chancellor replied: "He was precisely chosen from among the attendants to become a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " The right chancellor answered, "He was indeed selected from the attendants to serve as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 」帝奇之，曰：「斯人可用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor marveled and said: "This man can be used.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was impressed and said, "This man is worth employing.

sentences.zh: 」明日，擢為大都路治中。

translations.literal: " The next day, he was promoted to Administrative Vice-Director of the Dadu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Siming was promoted to Administrative Vice-Director of the Dadu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 思明以超遷逾等，固辭，乃改湖廣行省都事。

translations.literal: Siming, because the promotion skipped ranks and exceeded proper grade, firmly declined, and was then changed to Chief Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Siming declined the appointment on the grounds that the promotion skipped too many ranks, and was instead appointed Chief Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，召為中書省檢校，六曹無滯案，遷戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, he was summoned as Inspector of the Central Secretariat; in the six bureaus there were no stalled cases, and he was transferred to Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned to serve as inspector of the Central Secretariat, where he cleared all backlogged cases in the six bureaus and was promoted to section chief in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大德初，擢左司都事，有獻西域秤法，思明以惑眾不用。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dade, he was promoted to Chief Administrator of the Left Department; someone presented a Western Regions method of weighing, and Siming, deeming it would mislead the people, did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade reign he was promoted to chief administrator of the Left Department. When someone offered a new weighing method from the Western Regions, Siming refused to adopt it, believing it would mislead the public.

sentences.zh: 初立海道運糧萬戶府於江浙，受除者憚涉險，不行，思明請升等以優之，因著為令。

translations.literal: When the Maritime Grain Transport Wanhu Office was first established in Jiang-Zhe, those appointed feared the dangers of the route and did not take up their posts; Siming requested raising their rank to favor them, and this was written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Maritime Grain Transport Wanhu Office was first established in Jiang-Zhe, appointees were afraid of the perilous sea route and declined to serve. Siming petitioned to raise their rank as an incentive, and the policy was codified as a regulation.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，改集賢司直。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was changed to Direct Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reassigned as direct attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十年，除江浙行中書省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Director of the Left and Right Departments of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the left and right departments of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，兩浙大饑，首贊發廩賑之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, both Zhe regions suffered great famine; he was the first to advocate opening the granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year both Zhe regions suffered severe famine; he was the first to urge opening the public granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，遷兩浙鹽運使，未上，入參議樞密院事，改中書省左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, he was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe regions; before taking up the post he entered to deliberate on affairs of the Privy Council and was changed to Director of the Left Department of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhida he was appointed Salt Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhe regions, but before assuming the post he was called in to deliberate on Privy Council affairs and reassigned as director of the Left Department of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，再授兩浙鹽運使，歲課羨贏，僚屬請上增數，思明曰：「贏縮不常，萬一以增為額，是我希一己之榮，遺百世之害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, he was again appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe regions; the year's revenue exceeded the quota, and subordinates asked to report the increase; Siming said: "Surplus and shortfall are not constant; if by chance the increase were made the fixed quota, that would be my seeking personal glory and bequeathing harm for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing he was again appointed Salt Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhe regions. When annual revenue exceeded the quota, his staff urged reporting the higher figure. Siming said, "Surpluses and shortfalls are unpredictable; if we fixed the quota at the higher amount, I would be trading personal credit for lasting harm to the realm.

sentences.zh: 」二年，召為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: " In the second year, he was summoned as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year he was summoned to serve as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，進參議中書省事；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, he advanced to Deliberator of Central Secretariat Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was promoted to deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 三年，拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: in the third year, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and in the third year he was appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，浮屠妙總統有寵，敕中書官其弟五品，思明執不可。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, the Buddhist monk Miaozong had favor; an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to grant his younger brother a fifth-rank office, and Siming steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, the Buddhist monk Miaozong enjoyed imperial favor. An edict directed the Central Secretariat to grant his younger brother a fifth-rank office, but Siming firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，召見切責之，對曰：「選法，天下公器。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, summoned and sharply rebuked him; he replied: "The selection law is the common vessel of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and summoned him for a stern rebuke. Siming replied, "The selection system is a public instrument of the state.

sentences.zh: 徑路一開，來者雜遝。

translations.literal: Once a shortcut is opened, those who come will crowd in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once one back door is opened, a flood of petitioners will follow.

sentences.zh: 故寧違旨獲戾，不忍隳祖宗成憲，使四方得窺陛下淺深也。

translations.literal: Therefore I would rather disobey the edict and incur blame than destroy the established statutes of the ancestors and let the four quarters probe the depth of Your Majesty's will.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather defy your order and accept punishment than tear down the statutes our ancestors established and let the whole empire test how far your indulgence extends.

sentences.zh: 」帝心然其言，而業已許之，曰：「卿可姑與之，後勿為例。

translations.literal: " The Emperor inwardly approved his words, but having already promised, said: "You may for the moment grant it to him, but do not make it a precedent hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was persuaded in his heart, but having already given his word he said, "Grant it to him for now, but do not treat this as a precedent.

sentences.zh: 」乃為萬億庫提舉，不與散官。

translations.literal: " He was then made Superintendent of the Wanyi Treasury, without a regular rank title.
translations.idiomatic: " The brother was made superintendent of the Wanyi Treasury, without a regular civil rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，近臣疾其持法峭直，日構讒間，出為工部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time, close ministers resented his stern and upright enforcement of law and daily wove slander; he was sent out as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, court favorites resented his strict and upright enforcement of the law and daily spread slander against him; he was transferred out to serve as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝問左右曰：「張士瞻居工部，得無怏怏乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked those around him: "Zhang Shizhan at the Ministry of Works—surely he is not discontent?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his attendants, "Now that Zhang Shizhan is at the Ministry of Works, surely he is discontent?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「勤政如初。

translations.literal: " They replied: "He attends to duties as at first.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "He works as diligently as ever.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉嘆之，命授宣政院副使。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and sighed, and ordered him granted the post of Vice Commissioner of the Xuanzheng Commission.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor praised him warmly and appointed him vice commissioner of the Xuanzheng Commission.

sentences.zh: 五年，除西京宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed pacification commissioner of Xijing.

sentences.zh: 嶺北戍士多貧者，歲凶，相挺為變，思明威惠並行，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: Many garrison soldiers north of the passes were poor; in a bad year they banded together in mutiny; Siming combined authority and kindness, and the borderlands were then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Many frontier garrison soldiers north of the passes were destitute; in famine years they rose in mutiny. Siming combined firmness with kindness, and the border was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 因疏和林運糧不便事十一條，帝勞以端硯、上尊。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized eleven points on the inconveniences of transporting grain to Karakorum, and the Emperor rewarded him with an inkstone and fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial listing eleven problems with grain transport to Karakorum, and the Emperor rewarded him with an inkstone and fine wine.

sentences.zh: 會左丞相哈散辭職，帝不允，其請益堅，帝詰之曰：「朕任卿未專邪？

translations.literal: It happened that Left Chancellor Hasan resigned; the Emperor did not assent, but his request grew firmer; the Emperor interrogated him, saying: "Have I not entrusted you fully?
translations.idiomatic: When Left Chancellor Hasan sought to resign, the Emperor refused, but Hasan pressed his request. The Emperor questioned him: "Have I not given you my full trust?

translations.literal: " He said: "No.
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan answered, "No.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「近臣有撓政者邪？

translations.literal: " He said: "Are there close ministers interfering in government?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Are close ministers interfering in government?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「無有也。

translations.literal: " He said: "There are none.
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan replied, "None.

sentences.zh: 」「然則何為而辭？

translations.literal: " "Then why resign?
translations.idiomatic: " "Then why do you wish to resign?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣自揆才薄，恐誤陛下國事，若必欲任臣，願荐一人為助。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I judge my own talent thin and fear I may err in Your Majesty's state affairs; if you must employ me, I wish to recommend one man to assist.
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan answered, "I find my own talents inadequate and fear I may harm your affairs. If you insist on keeping me, I ask to recommend one man to assist me.

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「為誰？

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked: "Who?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor asked, "Who?

sentences.zh: 朕能從汝。

translations.literal: I can follow you.
translations.idiomatic: I will do as you say.

sentences.zh: 」哈散再拜謝曰；

translations.literal: " Hasan bowed again in thanks and said;
translations.idiomatic: " Hasan bowed again and said,

sentences.zh: 「臣願得張思明。

translations.literal: "I wish to obtain Zhang Siming.
translations.idiomatic: "I wish to have Zhang Siming.

sentences.zh: 」即日拜思明中書參知政事。

translations.literal: " That very day Siming was appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Siming was appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 比召至，車駕幸上都，見於道，慰勉之曰：「卿向不負朕注委，故朕用哈散言，復起汝。

translations.literal: By the time he was summoned and arrived, the imperial carriage was visiting Shangdu; he was received on the road; the Emperor comforted and encouraged him, saying: "You formerly did not fail my trust, therefore I have followed Hasan's words and raised you again.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he was summoned, the Emperor was traveling to Shangdu and received him on the road. The Emperor encouraged him, saying, "You never failed the trust I placed in you, so I have taken Hasan's advice and recalled you.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，升左丞。

translations.literal: " Before long, he was promoted to Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was promoted to left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，英宗宅憂，右丞相帖木迭兒用事，日誅大臣不附己者，中外洶洶。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, Yingzong was in mourning; Right Chancellor Temuder held power and daily executed great ministers who did not attach themselves to him; within and without there was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor's death, while Yingzong was still in mourning, Right Chancellor Temüder seized power and daily executed ministers who would not follow him, throwing court and country into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 思明諫曰：「山陵甫畢，新君未立，丞相恣行殺戮，國人皆謂陰有不臣之心。

translations.literal: Siming remonstrated, saying: "The imperial tomb has just been completed and the new ruler is not yet established; the chancellor wantonly carries out killings, and the people of the realm all say he secretly harbors disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Siming remonstrated, "The imperial tomb rites have only just ended and the new emperor is not yet enthroned. The chancellor is killing at will, and everyone in the realm suspects him of disloyal ambition.

sentences.zh: 萬一諸王駙馬疑而不至，將奈之何？

translations.literal: If by chance the princes and imperial sons-in-law doubt and do not come, what then can be done?
translations.idiomatic: If the princes and imperial sons-in-law grow suspicious and refuse to attend, what will you do then?

sentences.zh: 不可不熟慮也。

translations.literal: This cannot but be carefully considered.
translations.idiomatic: This must be weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆危之，帖木迭兒大悟曰：「非左丞言，幾誤吾事。

translations.literal: " All were alarmed for him; Temuder greatly awakened and said: "But for the left chancellor's words, I would nearly have ruined my affair.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone feared for him, but Temüder saw the point and said, "Had the left chancellor not spoken, I would nearly have ruined everything.

sentences.zh: 」帝造壽安山寺，監察御史觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失、成珪、李謙亨強諫，帝震怒，殺觀音保、瑣咬兒哈的迷失，以成珪、李謙亨屬吏，思明白丞相曰：「言事，御史職也，祖宗已來，未嘗殺諫臣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor built Shou'an Temple; Supervising Censor Guanyinbao, Suo'er Ha'di Shimi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated strongly; the Emperor was greatly angered and killed Guanyinbao and Suo'er Ha'di Shimi, and handed Cheng Gui and Li Qianheng over to the officials; Siming told the chancellor plainly: "Speaking out is the censor's duty; since the ancestors, remonstrating officials have never been killed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor ordered construction of Shou'an Temple, supervising censors Guanyinbao, Suo'er Ha'di Shimi, Cheng Gui, and Li Qianheng remonstrated forcefully. The Emperor was enraged and executed Guanyinbao and Suo'er Ha'di Shimi, turning Cheng Gui and Li Qianheng over to the courts. Siming told the chancellor plainly, "Remonstrance is the censor's duty; since the founding of the dynasty, no remonstrating official has been put to death.

sentences.zh: 」成、李既屬吏，當論法，丞相乃力言之，二人得從輕典。

translations.literal: " Cheng and Li having been handed to officials should be judged by law; the chancellor then spoke forcefully on their behalf, and the two men received lighter punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Cheng and Li were in the hands of the law, the chancellor argued strenuously on their behalf, and both received lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 及拜住為左丞相，與帖木迭兒各樹朋黨，賊害忠良，思明懼禍及，累表辭，不獲，後竟誣以不支蒙古子女口糧，餓死四百人，遂廢於家，杜門六年。

translations.literal: When Baiju became left chancellor and he and Temuder each formed factions and harmed the loyal and good, Siming feared disaster would reach him, repeatedly submitted memorials to resign without success, and was eventually falsely charged with failing to supply grain rations for Mongol men, women, and children, causing four hundred to starve to death; he was then dismissed and lived at home, closing his door for six years.
translations.idiomatic: When Baiju became left chancellor and he and Temüder each built factions and destroyed loyal ministers, Siming feared he would be caught up in the purge. He repeatedly petitioned to resign without success, and was eventually framed for failing to supply grain rations to four hundred Mongol men, women, and children who starved to death. He was dismissed and lived in seclusion at home for six years.

sentences.zh: 思明平生不治產，不畜財，收書三萬七千餘卷；

translations.literal: Throughout his life Siming did not manage property or accumulate wealth; he collected more than thirty-seven thousand scrolls of books;
translations.idiomatic: Siming never managed estates or hoarded wealth; he amassed more than thirty-seven thousand volumes in his library;

sentences.zh: 尤明於律，與謝仲和、曹鼎新同稱三絕。

translations.literal: he was especially expert in law, and together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin was called the Three Unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: he was especially masterful in law, and together with Xie Zhonghe and Cao Dingxin was known as the Three Unmatched.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠翊治守義功臣，依前中書左丞、上護軍、清河郡公，諡貞敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Merit Lord Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Governance, and Upholds Righteousness, retaining his former rank as Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat, Upper Guardian General, and Duke of Qinghe, with the posthumous name Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Merit Lord Who Promotes Loyalty, Assists Governance, and Upholds Righteousness, with his former titles of left chancellor of the Central Secretariat, upper guardian general, and Duke of Qinghe, and was given the posthumous name Zhenmin.

sentences.zh: ○吳元珪

translations.literal: ○ Wu Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wu Yuangui

sentences.zh: 吳元珪，字君璋，廣平人。

translations.literal: Wu Yuangui, courtesy name Junzhang, was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuangui, courtesy name Junzhang, was a native of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 父鼎，燕南提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: His father Ding was Deputy Intendant of the Yan-Nan Investigation and Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding served as deputy intendant of the Yan-Nan Investigation and Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 元珪簡重，好深沉之思，凡徵謀治法、律令章程，皆得於家庭之所授受。

translations.literal: Yuangui was simple and grave, fond of deep reflection; all matters of policy, law, statutes, and regulations he learned from what the family received and transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was reserved and dignified, with a taste for deep thought; he learned governance, law, and administrative procedure from what his family taught him at home.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖召見，命侍左右，授後衛經歷，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Kublai summoned and received him, ordered him to attend at his side, and appointed him Administrator of the Rear Guard, bestowing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Kublai summoned him, had him attend at court, appointed him administrator of the Rear Guard, and granted him a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 十七年，從幸上都，受命取禦藥於大都萬歲山，元珪乘傳，未盡一晝夜而至。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, following the imperial progress to Shangdu, he received orders to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu; Yuangui traveled by relay horse and arrived in less than one day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, while accompanying the court to Shangdu, he was ordered to fetch imperial medicine from Wansui Mountain in Dadu. Yuangui traveled by relay and arrived in less than a day and a night.

sentences.zh: 帝奇其速，擢樞密都事，升經歷。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at his speed and promoted him to Chief Administrator of the Privy Council, advancing him to Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled at his speed, promoted him to chief administrator of the Privy Council, and advanced him to full administrator.

sentences.zh: 嘗從同知樞密院事俺伯進西蕃鎧甲，帝問其制度，元珪應對詳明，帝益奇之。

translations.literal: He once followed Associate Administrator of the Privy Council Anbo in presenting Western Regions armor; the Emperor asked about its system, and Yuangui answered in detail and clearly; the Emperor was still more impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying Associate Administrator Anbo in presenting armor from the Western Regions, he answered the Emperor's questions about its design with detailed clarity, impressing the Emperor still further.

sentences.zh: 初，江南既定，樞密奏裁定官屬，京師五衛、行省、萬戶府設官有差，均俸祿，給醫藥，設學校，置屯田，多元珪所論建。

translations.literal: At first, when the south of the Yangtze was settled, the Privy Council memorialized to fix official establishments; the Five Guards of the capital, branch secretariats, and wanhu offices had differing official posts, equal salaries, provision of medicine, establishment of schools, and setting of garrison fields—much of this Yuangui proposed and established.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified, the Privy Council petitioned to standardize official establishments. The differing posts in the capital's five guards, branch secretariats, and wanhu offices; equalized salaries; medical provision; schools; and garrison farms—much of this was Yuangui's work.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he became Deliberator of Privy Council Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he became deliberator on Privy Council affairs.

sentences.zh: 時繕修宮城，尚書省奏役軍士萬人，留守司主之。

translations.literal: At the time the palace city was being repaired; the Ministry of Works memorialized to employ ten thousand soldiers, with the Office of the Capital Guard presiding.
translations.idiomatic: While the palace city was under repair, the Ministry of Works petitioned to conscript ten thousand soldiers under the Office of the Capital Guard.

sentences.zh: 元珪亟陳其不便，乃立武衛，繕理宮城，以留守段天祐兼都指揮使，凡有興作，必以聞於樞府。

translations.literal: Yuangui urgently stated its inconvenience; thereupon the Martial Guard was established to manage repair of the palace city, with Capital Guard Commissioner Duan Tianyou also serving as Commander-in-Chief; whenever there was construction, it had to be reported to the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui urgently argued against the plan. The Martial Guard was then established to manage palace repairs, with Capital Guard Commissioner Duan Tianyou also serving as commander-in-chief; all construction had to be reported to the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 尋升樞密院判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice director of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 奏定萬戶用軍士八人，千戶四人，百戶二人，多役者有罰。

translations.literal: He memorialized fixing that a wanhu might use eight soldiers, a qianhu four, and a baihu two; those who over-requisitioned labor were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized limits on corvée: a wanhu could use eight soldiers, a qianhu four, and a baihu two, with penalties for excess requisition.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，除禮部侍郎，遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to Director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed vice minister of rites and transferred to director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he became Deliberator of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he became deliberator on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 選曹銓注，多有私其鄉里者，元珪曰：「此風不可長，川黨、朔黨之興，宋之所由衰也。

translations.literal: In appointments the Selection Bureau often favored their own home districts; Yuangui said: "This practice must not be allowed to grow; the rise of Sichuan factions and northern factions was how Song declined.
translations.idiomatic: In making appointments the Selection Bureau often favored candidates from officials' home districts. Yuangui said, "This habit must not be indulged; factionalism between Sichuan and northern cliques was how the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 」請謁悉皆謝絕。

translations.literal: " He refused all requests for private audience.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused all private solicitations.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣撫燕南，劾貪吏若干人。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Pacification Commissioner of Yan-Nan, he impeached several corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while serving as pacification commissioner of Yan-Nan, he impeached several corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，河朔連年水旱，五穀不登，元珪言：「《春秋》之義，以養民為本，凡用民力者必書，蓋民力息則生養遂，生養遂則教化行而風俗美。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of Works; north of the Yellow River suffered consecutive years of flood and drought and the five grains did not ripen; Yuangui said: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals takes nourishing the people as fundamental; wherever the people's labor is used it must be recorded, for when the people's strength rests, sustenance is secure; when sustenance is secure, education proceeds and customs are refined.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed minister of works, he addressed years of flood and drought north of the Yellow River when crops failed. Yuangui said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that nourishing the people is fundamental; every use of labor must be recorded, for when the people rest they prosper, and when they prosper, education spreads and customs improve.

sentences.zh: 」宰相嘉其言，土木之工稍為之息。

translations.literal: " The chancellor praised his words, and construction work was somewhat halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The chancellor praised his argument, and construction projects were scaled back.

sentences.zh: 六年，僉河南行中書省事，將行，拜江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat; about to depart, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed associate administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, but before departing was instead made associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，硃清、張瑄以財雄江南，遍以金幣連結當路，及伏誅，錄其家，具籍所交諸公貴人，而江浙省臣為尤甚，惟元珪一無所污。

translations.literal: At first Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan, with wealth dominating Jiangnan, widely linked powerful men with gold and coin; when they were executed, their households were registered and all the great officials and nobles they had contacted were listed; the Jiang-Zhe provincial ministers were especially implicated, yet Yuangui alone was unstained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan had dominated Jiangnan through wealth, buying influence with gold and cash throughout the bureaucracy. When they were executed, the inventory of their contacts implicated many Jiang-Zhe officials—but Yuangui alone was untouched.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，由僉樞密院事拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, from Associate Administrator of the Privy Council he was appointed Vice Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Yuangui rose from associate administrator of the Privy Council to vice director.

sentences.zh: 詔元珪二十餘人議政中書，若惜人力，嚴選舉，節財用，定律令，謹賞罰，建科舉，課農桑，汰冗員，易封贈，皆切於世務者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuangui and more than twenty others to deliberate on government at the Central Secretariat—such matters as cherishing human labor, strict selection, economizing expenditures, fixing laws and statutes, careful rewards and punishments, establishing the civil service examinations, encouraging agriculture and sericulture, cutting redundant posts, and reforming enfeoffment and posthumous honors—all pressing on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yuangui and more than twenty others to advise the Central Secretariat on urgent matters of state: conserving labor, tightening appointments, cutting expenses, codifying law, enforcing discipline in rewards and punishments, restoring examinations, promoting farming and silk production, eliminating redundant posts, and reforming enfeoffments and posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 初，詔發軍萬人屯田稱海以實邊，海都之亂，被俘者眾，至是頗有來歸者，飢寒不能存，至鬻子以活。

translations.literal: At first an edict had sent ten thousand soldiers to garrison and farm at Chenghai to strengthen the border; in Haidu's rebellion many were captured; by this time many had returned, but cold and hunger left them unable to survive, even to the point of selling children to live.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had sent ten thousand soldiers to farm at Chenghai to strengthen the frontier. Many were captured in Haidu's rebellion; by now many had returned, but hunger and cold drove some to sell their children to survive.

sentences.zh: 元珪具其事以聞，詔賜錢贖之。

translations.literal: Yuangui fully reported the matter; an edict granted money to redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui reported the situation in full, and the court issued funds to redeem the children.

sentences.zh: 帝在軍中，即聞元珪名，至是，特加平章政事，賜白金二百五十兩、只孫衣四襲。

translations.literal: The Emperor, while in the army, had already heard Yuangui's name; at this time he was specially added as Grand Councillor, and granted two hundred fifty taels of white silver and four sets of zisun robes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had heard of Yuangui's reputation even while campaigning; now he was specially promoted to grand councillor and granted two hundred fifty taels of silver and four sets of zisun robes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，詔元珪與十六人議時政。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, an edict ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to deliberate on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he ordered Yuangui and sixteen others to advise on current policy.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，出拜江浙行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, he was sent out and appointed Left Chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing he was appointed left chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江淮漕臣言：「江南殷富，蓋由多匿腴田，若再行檢覆之法，當益田畝累萬計。

translations.literal: An official of the Jiang-Huai grain transport said: "Jiangnan is rich and prosperous, largely because many fertile fields are concealed; if the method of re-inspection and verification is again applied, field acreage should increase by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiang-Huai grain transport official said, "Jiangnan's wealth comes largely from hidden fertile fields; if we reintroduce land verification, registered acreage should increase by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 」元珪曰：「江南之平，幾四十年，戶有定籍，田有定畝，一有動搖，其害不細。

translations.literal: " Yuangui said: "Since Jiangnan was pacified, nearly forty years have passed; households have fixed registers and fields fixed acreage; once this is disturbed, the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuangui replied, "Jiangnan has been at peace for nearly forty years; households and fields have fixed registers. Disturb that system and the harm will be grave.

sentences.zh: 」執其論固爭，月餘不能止，移疾去。

translations.literal: " Holding to his argument he firmly contended; for more than a month he could not be stopped, and he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " He held to his view and argued stubbornly for over a month until, unable to prevail, he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，拜甘肅行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, he was appointed Left Chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was appointed left chancellor of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召還，俾宣撫遼陽諸郡，復為樞密副使，召見嘉禧殿，帝曰：「卿先朝舊臣，宜在舊服。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled, made to pacify the commanderies of Liaodong, and again became Vice Director of the Privy Council; summoned and received in Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said: "You are an old minister of the previous reign and should wear your former rank.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was recalled, sent to pacify the commanderies of Liaodong, and again made vice director of the Privy Council. Summoned to Jiaxi Hall, the Emperor said, "You are a veteran of the previous reign and should hold your former station.

sentences.zh: 」特加榮祿大夫，賜鈔五千緡、貂裘二襲。

translations.literal: " He was specially granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, five thousand strings of paper money, and two sable fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: " He was specially granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, five thousand strings of paper money, and two sable fur coats.

sentences.zh: 元珪奏曰：「昔世祖限田四百畝，以給軍需，餘田悉貢賦稅。

translations.literal: Yuangui memorialized, saying: "Formerly Kublai limited fields to four hundred mu to supply military needs; all remaining fields paid tribute and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui memorialized, "In Kublai's day military fields were capped at four hundred mu; all other land paid regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 今經理江淮田土，第以增金為能，加以有司頭會箕斂，俾元元之民，困苦日甚，臣恐變生不測，非國之福，惟陛下少加意焉。

translations.literal: Now in managing Jiang-Huai fields, success is measured only by increased revenue; moreover officials squeeze and exact layer upon layer, making the common people daily more distressed; I fear unforeseen change may arise—not the realm's blessing; may Your Majesty give this a little attention.
translations.idiomatic: Now in reassessing Jiang-Huai land, officials are judged only by how much revenue they add, and local magistrates squeeze the people ever harder. I fear unrest may follow—not a blessing to the state. I beg Your Majesty to take heed.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「凡爾軍士之田，並遵舊制。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "All fields of you soldiers shall follow the old system."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor replied, "All military fields shall follow the old system."

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，元珪與知樞密院事帖木兒不花上軍民之政十餘事，大抵言：諸王近侍，不可干軍政；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, when Yingzong took the throne, Yuangui together with Privy Council Administrator Temur Buqa submitted more than ten items on military and civilian administration, broadly stating: princes and close attendants must not interfere in military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi, when Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Yuangui and Privy Council Administrator Temür Buqa submitted more than ten recommendations on military and civilian administration, chief among them that princes and close attendants must not interfere in military affairs;

sentences.zh: 管軍官吏，不可漁取軍戶；

translations.literal: military officers must not plunder military households;
translations.idiomatic: military administrators must not prey on military households;

sentences.zh: 軍官之材者，當遷其職；

translations.literal: officers of talent should be transferred to appropriate posts;
translations.idiomatic: capable officers should be promoted to suitable posts;

sentences.zh: 有司賦役，當務均一，而軍民不可有所偏；

translations.literal: official levies and corvée should strive for uniformity, and soldiers and civilians must not be treated with partiality;
translations.idiomatic: taxes and corvée must be applied evenly, without favoring either soldiers or civilians;

sentences.zh: 軍官襲職，惟傳嫡嗣，而支庶不可有所亂。

translations.literal: in hereditary military office, only the direct heir should succeed, and collateral lines must not be allowed to disrupt the order.
translations.idiomatic: hereditary military posts should pass only to direct heirs, without collateral lines disrupting succession.

sentences.zh: 帝並嘉納，即降旨施行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor all praised and accepted them, and immediately issued edicts to put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved all of these and immediately issued edicts to implement them.

sentences.zh: 元珪以年老致仕，至治二年，起商議中書省事。

translations.literal: Yuangui retired on account of old age; in the second year of Zhizhi he was recalled to Deliberator of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui retired due to age; in the second year of Zhizhi he was recalled as deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，贈光祿大夫、河南等處行省平章政事、柱國，追封趙國公，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, grand councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 三年，復加推誠佐理功臣、光祿大夫、司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was further granted Merit Lord Who Sincerely Assists in Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was further granted Merit Lord Who Sincerely Assists in Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: ○張昇

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Sheng
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Sheng

sentences.zh: 張昇，字伯高，其先定州人，後徙平州。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Bogao, his ancestors were men of Dingzhou and later moved to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Bogao, came from a family originally of Dingzhou who later settled in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 升幼警敏過人，學語時，輒能辨字音，應對異於常兒；

translations.literal: Sheng in youth was alert and clever beyond others; when learning to speak he could distinguish word sounds, and his responses differed from ordinary children;
translations.idiomatic: As a child Sheng was unusually quick-witted; even while learning to speak he could distinguish tones, and his replies were unlike those of other children;

sentences.zh: 既長，力學，工文辭。

translations.literal: when grown, he studied hard and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: when grown he studied diligently and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，用薦者授將仕郎、翰林國史院編修官，預修《世祖實錄》。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, through recommendation he was appointed Gentleman for Initial Appointment and Compiler of the Hanlin Academy and National History Office, participating in compiling the Veritable Records of Kublai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation he was appointed compiler of the Hanlin Academy and National History Office and helped compile the Veritable Records of Kublai.

sentences.zh: 升應奉翰林文字，尋升修撰，歷興文署令，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Sheng served as Hanlin Documenter; soon he was promoted to Compiler, served as Director of the Office for Promoting Literature, and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng served as Hanlin documenter, was soon promoted to compiler, then director of the Office for Promoting Literature, and finally erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，大臣承中旨，議奉徽號，饗宗廟，升曰：「在故典，凡有事於宗廟，必書嗣皇帝名，今將何書？

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, great ministers acting on the inner court's intent deliberated on presenting a posthumous title and offering at the ancestral temple; Sheng said: "According to former precedent, whenever there is business at the ancestral temple, the name of the succeeding emperor must be written—what shall be written now?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzong died, ministers acting on the inner court's wishes debated presenting a posthumous title and offering at the ancestral temple. Sheng said, "By established precedent, any temple rite must record the succeeding emperor's name—what name should we write now?

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: " The deliberation was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，議躬祀禮，升據經引古，參酌時宜以對，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne, in deliberating on the rite of personal sacrifice, Sheng cited the classics and antiquity and weighed current appropriateness in reply; the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Sheng drew on the classics and historical precedent to advise on the rite of personal sacrifice, and the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 至大初，改太常寺為太常禮儀院，即除升為判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhida, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was changed to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual, and Sheng was immediately appointed Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhida reign the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was reorganized as the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual, and Sheng was appointed its vice director.

sentences.zh: 久之，外補知汝寧府。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed outside the capital as Prefect of Runing.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted outside the capital as prefect of Runing.

sentences.zh: 民有告寄束書於其家者，逾三年取閱，有禁書一編，且記里中大家姓名於上，升亟呼吏焚其書，曰：「妄言誣民，且再更赦矣，勿論。

translations.literal: A commoner reported that a bundle of books had been deposited at his house; after more than three years he took them out to read and found one volume of prohibited books, with the names of leading families in the district recorded on it; Sheng immediately called clerks to burn the book and said: "False words slander the people, and there have already been two general amnesties—do not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: A local man reported that a bundle of books had been left at his home; more than three years later Sheng opened it and found a volume of banned books listing prominent local families. He immediately ordered it burned, saying, "This is malicious slander, and two general amnesties have already passed—let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 」同列懼，皆引起。

translations.literal: " Colleagues were alarmed and all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " His colleagues were alarmed and all fell silent.

sentences.zh: 既而事聞，廷議謂升脫姦軌，遣使窮問，卒無跡可指，乃詰以擅焚書狀，升對曰：「事固類姦軌，然升備位郡守，為民父母，今斥誣訴，免冤濫，雖重得罪不避。

translations.literal: Soon the matter was reported; court deliberation held that Sheng had shielded treasonous plots and sent envoys to investigate thoroughly; in the end no trace could be found, and he was then charged with burning books on his own authority; Sheng replied: "The matter indeed resembled treason, yet Sheng occupies the post of prefect and is father and mother to the people; now rejecting false accusation and sparing the innocent, though I should heavily offend I do not avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached court, some argued he had shielded treason and investigators were sent; no evidence was found, but he was charged with unauthorized destruction of evidence. Sheng replied, "It did look like treason, but as prefect I am guardian of the people. I would rather face punishment than let false accusations ruin innocent lives.

sentences.zh: 」乃坐奪俸二月。

translations.literal: " He was therefore penalized by deducting two months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: " He was penalized with two months' forfeiture of salary.

sentences.zh: 旁郡移文報吳人侯君遠者言：「歲直壬子六月朔日蝕，其占為兵寇；

translations.literal: A neighboring prefecture sent documents reporting a man of Wu named Hou Junyuan, saying: "In the year renzi on the first day of the sixth month there was an eclipse; its omen is soldiers and bandits;
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring prefecture reported that a Wu man named Hou Junyuan had predicted, "In the year renzi, a solar eclipse on the first day of the sixth month foretells war and invasion;

sentences.zh: 歲癸丑，其應在吳分野。

translations.literal: in the year guichou, the response should be in the Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: in the year guichou the omen will fall on the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 」同列欲召屬縣為備禦計，升曰：「此訛言，久當自息，毋用惑民聽。

translations.literal: " Colleagues wished to summon the subordinate districts to prepare defenses; Sheng said: "This is false rumor; in time it will cease of itself—do not use it to alarm the people.
translations.idiomatic: " Colleagues wanted to mobilize the districts for defense. Sheng said, "This is baseless rumor that will die out on its own—do not alarm the people.

sentences.zh: 」斥其無稽，眾論韙之。

translations.literal: " He rejected it as groundless, and public opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismissed it as unfounded, and others agreed.

sentences.zh: 部使者舉治行為諸郡最。

translations.literal: The regional inspector reported his governance as foremost among the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspector ranked his governance first among all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歷江西行省左右司郎中，除紹興路總管。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Left and Right Departments of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed Chief Administrator of the Shaoxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the left and right departments of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was appointed chief administrator of the Shaoxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，大德、至大間，越大饑，且疫癘，民死者殆半，賦稅鹽課責里胥代納，吏並緣為奸，害富家，升為證於簿籍，白行省蠲之。

translations.literal: At first, between the Dade and Zhida reigns, Yue suffered great famine and pestilence; nearly half the people died; tax and salt levies were charged to village headmen for payment, and clerks used this as pretext for corruption, harming wealthy families; Sheng verified against the registers and reported to the branch secretariat for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade and Zhida reigns Shaoxing suffered famine and plague that killed nearly half the population. Tax and salt assessments were shifted onto village headmen, and clerks exploited the system to extort the wealthy. Sheng verified the records and petitioned the branch secretariat for relief.

sentences.zh: 前守有為江浙行省參知政事者，爭代者祿米，有隙，欲內之罪，移平江歲輸海運糧布囊三萬，俾紹興制如數，民患苦之，不能堪。

translations.literal: A former prefect had become Associate Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; disputing replacement grain stipends, there was a rift; wishing to trap him in crime, he shifted thirty thousand sacks of maritime transport grain from Pingjiang for Shaoxing to produce in equal number; the people suffered bitterly and could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: A former prefect had become associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat. After a dispute over grain stipends, he tried to ruin Sheng by transferring thirty thousand sacks of maritime transport grain from Pingjiang onto Shaoxing's account; the people could not endure the burden.

sentences.zh: 更數守，謂歲例如此，置弗問。

translations.literal: Several successive prefects said the annual precedent was thus and set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Several successive prefects accepted it as annual precedent and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 升言：「麻非越土所生，海漕實吳郡事，於越無與。

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Hemp is not native to Yue soil; maritime transport is truly a Wu commandery affair and has nothing to do with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng argued, "Hemp is not produced in Yue; maritime transport is a Wu affair and has nothing to do with us.

sentences.zh: 」章上，卒罷之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, in the end it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " His memorial prevailed and the levy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 升既謹於繩吏，又果於去民瘼，故人心悅服。

translations.literal: Sheng was both strict in binding officials and resolute in removing the people's afflictions; therefore the people's hearts were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was strict with officials and resolute in removing the people's burdens, winning broad popular support.

sentences.zh: 歷湖北道廉訪使、江南行台治書侍御史，召為參議中書省事，改樞密院判官，尋復中書參議。

translations.literal: He served as Surveillance Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit and Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was summoned as Deliberator of Central Secretariat Affairs, was changed to Vice Director of the Privy Council, and soon again Deliberator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as surveillance commissioner of Hubei and investigating censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, was summoned as deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs, then vice director of the Privy Council, and soon again deliberator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，又出為河東道廉訪使，未行，拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, he was again sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit; before departing he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Hedong; before departing he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: The next year, he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Huai-West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，拜陝西行省參知政事，加中奉大夫，尋遷遼東道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding, he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, granted Grand Master for Promoting Governance, and soon transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding he was appointed associate administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat with the title Grand Master for Promoting Governance, and soon transferred to surveillance commissioner of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 屬永平大水，民多捐瘠，升請發海道糧十八萬石、鈔五萬緡，以賑饑民，且蠲其歲賦，朝廷從之，民得全活者眾。

translations.literal: It happened that Yongping suffered great flood; many people were emaciated; Sheng requested issuing one hundred eighty thousand shi of maritime transport grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money to relieve the hungry people, and also exempting their year's tax; the court followed this, and many people were wholly preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongping suffered severe flooding and many were starving, Sheng petitioned for one hundred eighty thousand shi of maritime grain and fifty thousand strings of paper money for relief, plus exemption from that year's taxes. The court agreed, saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜侍御史。

translations.literal: The next year, he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，出為山東道廉訪使，時方有警，有司請完城以為備，升曰：「民恃吾以生，完城是棄民也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli, he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit; at the time there was an alarm, and officials requested completing the city walls for defense; Sheng said: "The people rely on us for life—completing the walls is abandoning the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianli reign he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Shandong. With unrest in the region, officials wanted to fortify the city walls. Sheng said, "The people depend on us for survival—to fortify the walls is to abandon them.

sentences.zh: 」由是民皆安之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the people were all reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " The people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 文宗賜尚醖文幣，以賞其功。

translations.literal: Wenzong bestowed imperial wine and silk to reward his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong rewarded him with imperial wine and silk.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召為太禧院副使，兼奉贊神御殿事，除河南省左丞，复遷淮西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: After a year, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, concurrently in charge of the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, appointed Left Chancellor of Henan Province, and again transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of the Huai-West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Blessings, concurrently overseeing the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, appointed left chancellor of Henan Province, and again posted as surveillance commissioner of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 升時年六十有九，上書乞致仕。

translations.literal: Sheng was then sixty-nine and submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was then sixty-nine and petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，復起為集賢侍講學士，文宗眷待之意甚隆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun, he was again raised as Attendant Reader of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; Wenzong's favor and treatment were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun he was recalled as attendant reader of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; Emperor Wenzong treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，順帝即位，首詔在廷耆艾，訪問治道，升條上時所宜先者十事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, when Shundi took the throne, an edict first summoned the aged at court to inquire about the way of governance; Sheng listed ten matters that should be prioritized at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong, when Emperor Shundi ascended the throne, he summoned elder statesmen to advise on governance; Sheng submitted ten priorities for the age.

sentences.zh: 尋兼經筵官，廷試進士，特命升讀卷，事已，告省先墓。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Lecturer at the Classics Mat, and at the palace examination for jinshi he was specially ordered to read the papers; when the affair was finished, he requested leave to visit his ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as lecturer at the Classics Mat, and at the palace examination was specially ordered to read the candidates' papers. When the examination ended, he asked leave to visit his family's graves.

sentences.zh: 帝賜金織文袍，以寵其歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a gold-woven robe to honor his return.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted him a gold-woven robe to honor his return home.

sentences.zh: 明年，以奎章閣大學士、資善大夫、知經筵事召，賜上尊，趣就職，升以疾辭。

translations.literal: The next year, he was summoned as Grand Academician of the Kui-Zhang Pavilion, Grand Master for Governance, and Director of the Classics Mat; fine wine was bestowed and he was urged to take office; Sheng declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned as grand academician of the Kui-Zhang Pavilion with the titles Grand Master for Governance and director of the Classics Mat. The Emperor sent fine wine and pressed him to serve, but Sheng declined citing illness.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不可強，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw he could not be forced and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not be persuaded, the Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 尋命本郡月給祿半，以終其身。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to receive half his monthly salary in his home district for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted half salary from his home district for life.

sentences.zh: 至正元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhizheng at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、河南等處行中書省左丞，諡文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and Left Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Master for Assisting Virtue and left chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 臧夢解陸垕

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie Lu Hao
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie and Lu Hao

sentences.zh: 臧夢解，慶元人，宋末中進士第，未官而國亡。

translations.literal: Zang Mengjie was a man of Qingyuan; in the late Song he passed the jinshi examination, but before taking office the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Mengjie was a native of Qingyuan who passed the jinshi examination in late Song, but before he could take office the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，從其鄉郡守將內附，授奉訓大夫、婺州路軍民人匠提舉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, he followed his home district's prefect-general in submitting to the dynasty and was appointed Grand Master for Promoting Instruction and Superintendent of Military and Artisan Households of Wuzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan he followed his district's prefect in surrendering to the Yuan and was appointed superintendent of military and artisan households of Wuzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，例革其所司，而浙東宣慰司舉夢解才兼儒吏，可試州郡，朝廷是之，授息州知州。

translations.literal: Before long, by regulation his office was abolished; the Zhe-Dong Pacification Commission recommended Mengjie as talented in both Confucian learning and administration and fit to be tried in a prefecture or district; the court approved and appointed him Prefect of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his office was abolished by regulation, but the Zhe-Dong Pacification Commission recommended Mengjie as skilled in both scholarship and administration. The court agreed and appointed him prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改知海寧州。

translations.literal: Before departing, he was changed to Prefect of Haining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was reassigned as prefect of Haining.

sentences.zh: 時淮東按察副使王慶之按行至其州，見夢解剛直廉慎，而學有淵奧，自任職以來，門無私謁，官署蕭然，凡有差役，皆當其貧富，而吏無所預。

translations.literal: At the time Deputy Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of Huai-Dong was on inspection tour in the prefecture; seeing Mengjie upright, incorrupt, and cautious, with learning of profound depth, since taking office there had been no private callers at his gate, the official quarters were austere, and whenever there were corvée assignments he matched rich and poor appropriately while clerks had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qingzhi of Huai-Dong inspected the prefecture and found Mengjie upright, incorruptible, and learned. Since taking office his gate had seen no private callers, his office was austere, and corvée duties were assigned according to each household's means without clerkly interference.

sentences.zh: 於是民以戶計者，新增七百六十有四；

translations.literal: Thereupon households by count newly increased by seven hundred sixty-four;
translations.idiomatic: Registered households increased by seven hundred sixty-four;

sentences.zh: 田以頃計者，新辟四百四十有三；

translations.literal: fields by qing newly opened by four hundred forty-three;
translations.idiomatic: newly opened fields by four hundred forty-three qing;

sentences.zh: 桑柘榆柳，交廕境內，而政平訟簡，為諸州縣最。

translations.literal: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow interlaced shade within the borders, and governance was peaceful and lawsuits few—foremost among prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: mulberry, catalpa, elm, and willow shaded the land; governance was peaceful and lawsuits rare—the best record among prefectures and districts.

sentences.zh: 乃舉夢解才德兼備，宜擢清要，以展所蘊。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Mengjie as complete in talent and virtue and fit to be promoted to a key post to display what he contained.
translations.idiomatic: Wang therefore recommended Mengjie as a man of complete talent and virtue worthy of a key appointment.

sentences.zh: 而御史臺亦以其廉能，抗章薦之。

translations.literal: The Censorate also, for his integrity and ability, submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate also memorialized recommending him for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，夢解滿去者至是已五年矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, those whose terms as prefect Mengjie had completed—it was now five years.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year, five years had passed since Mengjie completed his term as prefect.

sentences.zh: 屬江陰飢，江浙行省委夢解賑之。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiangyin suffered famine; the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangyin suffered famine, the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat commissioned Mengjie to administer relief.

sentences.zh: 夢解不為文具，皆躬至其地，而人給以米，所活四萬五千餘人。

translations.literal: Mengjie did not make empty documents; all went in person to the places, and each person was given rice; those preserved alive numbered more than forty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie dispensed with empty paperwork, went personally to each place, and distributed rice; more than forty-five thousand people were saved.

sentences.zh: 江南行台治書侍御史苟宗道，聞而韙之，舉其名上聞，除同知桂陽路總管府事。

translations.literal: Jiangnan Branch Censorate Investigating Censor Gou Zongdao, hearing of it, approved, and submitted his name to the throne; he was appointed Associate Chief Administrator of the Guiyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Gou Zongdao of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate approved and reported his name to the throne; Mengjie was appointed associate chief administrator of the Guiyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢奉議大夫、廣西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he was promoted to Grand Master for Discussion of Governance and Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangxi Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Guangxi Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.

sentences.zh: 故事，煙瘴之地，行部者多不躬至，而夢解咸遍歷焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, in malarial regions many on inspection tour did not go in person, but Mengjie all thoroughly visited them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, officials inspecting malarial regions often did not go in person, but Mengjie visited every one.

sentences.zh: 遂按問賓州、藤州兩路達魯花赤，與凡貪官姦吏，置於法者無慮八十餘人。

translations.literal: He then investigated and questioned the darughachi of Bin and Teng prefectures and all corrupt and wicked officials; those placed under the law numbered no fewer than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated the darughachi of Bin and Teng prefectures and corrupt officials alike, punishing no fewer than eighty.

sentences.zh: 又平反邕州黃震被誣贓罪，及藤州唐氏婦被誣殺夫罪，凡兩冤獄。

translations.literal: He also reversed the false charge of embezzlement against Huang Zhen of Yongzhou and the false charge of murdering her husband against a woman of the Tang clan of Tengzhou—two wrongful cases in all.
translations.idiomatic: He also reversed two wrongful convictions: the embezzlement charge against Huang Zhen of Yongzhou and the charge that a Tang-clan woman of Tengzhou had murdered her husband.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遷江西肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, he was transferred to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Jiangxi Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.

sentences.zh: 有臨江路總管李倜，素狡獪，而又附大臣勢，以控持省憲，夢解按其贓罪，而一道澄清。

translations.literal: There was Chief Administrator Li Tong of Linjiang Circuit, by nature cunning and moreover relying on a great minister's power to control the provincial surveillance officials; Mengjie investigated his embezzlement and the whole circuit was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Li Tong of Linjiang was cunning and backed by a powerful minister's influence over provincial officials. Mengjie prosecuted his embezzlement and cleared the whole circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷浙東肅政廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Zhe-Dong Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Zhe-Dong Commission.

sentences.zh: 九年，除廣東肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Commission for Upholding Governance and Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed surveillance commissioner of the Guangdong Commission.

sentences.zh: 夢解至是，既老且病，乃納祿退居杭州，以亞中大夫、湖南宣慰副使致仕。

translations.literal: Mengjie by this time was both old and ill; he returned his salary and retired to Hangzhou, retiring with the rank of Grand Master for the Palace and Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mengjie was old and ill; he surrendered his salary and retired to Hangzhou with the rank of deputy pacification commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 後至元元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Houzhiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Houzhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 夢解博學洽聞，為時名儒，然不少迂腐，而敏於政事，其操守尤為介特。

translations.literal: Mengjie was broadly learned and well informed, a famous Confucian of the age, yet not at all pedantic, and quick in administrative affairs; his integrity was especially uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie was broadly learned and renowned as a Confucian scholar, yet never pedantic and adept in administration; his integrity was especially uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 所著書，有《周官考》三卷、《春秋微》一卷。

translations.literal: Books he authored include three scrolls of Examination of the Rites of Zhou and one scroll of Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Examination of the Rites of Zhou in three scrolls and Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals in one scroll.

sentences.zh: 夢解嘗自號魯山大夫，士之稱之者，不以官，皆曰魯山先生云。

translations.literal: Mengjie once styled himself Great Officer of Lushan; scholars who spoke of him, not using his office, all called him Master Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengjie styled himself Great Officer of Lushan; scholars referred to him not by rank but as Master Lushan.

sentences.zh: 同時有陸垕者，與夢解齊名。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Lu Hao, equally famous with Mengjie.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Lu Hao, equally renowned with Mengjie.

sentences.zh: 監察御史鄭鵬南嘗以二人並薦於朝。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended the two men together to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Zheng Pengnan once recommended both men to the court.

sentences.zh: 垕字仁重，江陰人也。

translations.literal: Hao, courtesy name Renzhong, was a man of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hao, courtesy name Renzhong, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 自幼以孝友聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 至元間，丞相伯顏以師南下，垕是時年未冠，而志強氣銳，率其鄉人見之，論議有合，兵遂不涉其境，鄉人義之。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan period, Chancellor Bayan led the army south; Hao was then not yet capped, yet ambitious and spirited; he led his townspeople to see him; their discussion accorded, and the army therefore did not enter his territory; the townspeople honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan period, when Chancellor Bayan marched south, Hao was still a youth but bold in spirit. He led his townspeople to meet Bayan; their talks went well, and the army did not enter his district. The people honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 伯顏奏授為同知徽州路總管府事，以廉能擢置台憲，累遷至湖南肅政廉訪副使，升浙西廉訪使。

translations.literal: Bayan memorialized and appointed him Associate Chief Administrator of the Huizhou Circuit; for integrity and ability he was promoted to surveillance posts, rising to Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Hunan and then Surveillance Commissioner of Zhe-West.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan recommended him as associate chief administrator of Huizhou Circuit. For integrity and ability he rose through surveillance posts to deputy surveillance commissioner of Hunan and then surveillance commissioner of Zhe-West.

sentences.zh: 所至以黜贓吏、洗冤獄為己任，且嘗上章奏免儒役，及舉行浙西助役法。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, dismissing corrupt officials and clearing wrongful cases were his own charge; he also once memorialized to exempt Confucian corvée and to implement the Zhe-West corvée-assistance law.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, dismissing corrupt officials and clearing wrongful cases were his mission; he also memorialized to exempt Confucian corvée and to implement the Zhe-West corvée-assistance law.

sentences.zh: 年五十卒，賜諡莊簡。

translations.literal: He died at fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty and was granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 陳顥，字仲明，其先居盧龍，有名山者，仕金為謀克監軍，太祖得之，以為平陽等路軍民都元帥，子孫徙清州，遂為清州人。

translations.literal: Chen Hao, courtesy name Zhongming, his ancestors dwelt at Lulong; one named Mingshan served Jin as a company commander supervising troops; Taizu obtained him and made him Military and Civilian Commander-in-Chief of Pingyang and other circuits; descendants moved to Qingzhou and thus became men of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao, courtesy name Zhongming, came from a family originally of Lulong. An ancestor named Mingshan served the Jin as a company commander; Genghis Khan took him into service and made him commander-in-chief of Pingyang and other circuits. The family later moved to Qingzhou and became Qingzhou natives.

sentences.zh: 顥幼穎悟，日記誦千百言，稍長，遊京師，登翰林承旨王磐、安藏之門。

translations.literal: Hao in youth was quick-witted; each day he memorized and recited a thousand or more words; when somewhat grown he traveled to the capital and entered the gates of Hanlin Chancellor Wang Pan and An Zang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was bright as a boy and memorized a thousand or more characters daily. As a young man he went to the capital and studied under Hanlin Chancellor Wang Pan and An Zang.

sentences.zh: 磐熟金典章，安藏通諸國語，顥兼習之。

translations.literal: Pan was versed in Jin statutes and regulations; An Zang was versed in the languages of the various states; Hao studied both.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pan knew Jin law and institutions; An Zang knew the languages of the various states; Hao studied both.

sentences.zh: 安藏乃薦顥入宿衛，尋為仁宗潛邸說書。

translations.literal: An Zang then recommended Hao to enter the palace guard; soon he became Lecturer at Renzong's princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: An Zang recommended Hao for palace guard service; he soon became lecturer at Prince Renzong's household.

sentences.zh: 於是，仁宗奉母后出居懷慶，顥從行，日開陳以古聖賢居艱貞之道。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renzong, following the empress dowager, went out to dwell at Huaqing; Hao followed on the journey; daily he opened and set forth the way of the ancient sages in dwelling in hardship and maintaining integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong accompanied the empress dowager to live at Huaqing, Hao went with him and daily expounded how the ancient sages endured hardship and held to integrity.

sentences.zh: 會成宗崩，仁宗入定內難，以迎武宗，顥皆預謀。

translations.literal: It happened that Chengzong died; Renzong settled the inner turmoil and went to welcome Wuzong; Hao all took part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong resolved the succession crisis and went to welcome Wuzong; Hao took part in the planning throughout.

sentences.zh: 及仁宗即位，以推戴舊勳，特拜集賢大學士、榮祿大夫，仍宿衛禁中，政事無不與聞。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was specially appointed Grand Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, still serving in the palace guard within the forbidden precincts; in government affairs there was nothing he did not hear.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Hao was specially appointed grand academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness for his role in the succession, remaining on palace guard duty with access to all state affairs.

sentences.zh: 科舉之行，顥贊助之力尤多。

translations.literal: In the implementation of the civil service examinations, Hao's assisting effort was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil service examinations were restored, Hao's contribution was especially great.

sentences.zh: 顥時伺帝燕閒，輒取聖經所載大經大法有切治體者陳之，每見嘉納。

translations.literal: Hao often waited for the Emperor's leisure at ease, then took from the classics the great principles and fundamental laws bearing on governance and set them forth; each time he was praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Hao often waited for the Emperor's leisure and then expounded great principles from the classics relevant to governance; the Emperor always welcomed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗坐便殿，群臣入奏事，望見顥，喜曰：「陳仲明在列，所奏必善事矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor once sat in the informal hall; when the ministers entered to report affairs and saw Hao, he rejoiced and said: "Chen Zhongming is in the ranks—the matters reported will surely be good affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as ministers entered the informal hall to report business, the Emperor saw Hao and said with pleasure, "With Chen Zhongming present, whatever is reported will be worth hearing.

sentences.zh: 」顥以父年老，力請歸養清州，帝特命顥長子孝伯為知州以就養。

translations.literal: " Hao, because his father was old, strongly requested to return home to support him at Qingzhou; the Emperor specially ordered Hao's eldest son Xiaobo to be made prefect so he could be near for support.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hao's father grew old, he begged leave to return to Qingzhou to care for him. The Emperor specially appointed Hao's eldest son Xiaobo prefect so the family could be together.

sentences.zh: 顥固辭，乃以孝伯為州判官。

translations.literal: Hao firmly declined, and Xiaobo was then made Vice Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Hao declined the honor, and Xiaobo was made vice prefect instead.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用顥為中書平章政事，顥叩首謝曰：「臣無汗馬之功，又乏經濟之略，一旦置之政途，徒速臣咎。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to use Hao as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat; Hao kowtowed in thanks and said: "Your subject has no merit of sweat and horse, and also lacks strategy for ordering the state; once placed on the path of government, I would only hasten blame upon your subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to appoint Hao grand councillor of the Central Secretariat. Hao kowtowed and said, "I have no military merit and no talent for governing; if placed in high office I would only bring blame upon myself.

sentences.zh: 臣願得朝夕左右，獻替可否，庶少裨萬一，亦以全臣愚忠。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to obtain being at Your Majesty's side morning and evening, offering approval or rejection, hoping to benefit slightly in the least degree, and also to preserve your subject's foolish loyalty whole.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather stay at your side day and night, advising on what should be accepted or rejected, hoping to serve in some small way and preserve my humble loyalty intact.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃允。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，辭祿家居者十年。

translations.literal: When Renzong died, he resigned his salary and lived at home for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After Renzong's death he resigned his salary and lived in retirement for ten years.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，復起為集賢大學士，上疏勸帝大興文治、增國子學弟子員、蠲儒之徭役，文宗皆嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, he was again raised as Grand Academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; he submitted a memorial urging the Emperor to greatly promote literary governance, increase the number of students in the Directorate of Education, and exempt Confucians from corvée; Wenzong all praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, Hao was recalled as grand academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. He memorialized urging greater promotion of culture, more students in the Directorate of Education, and exemption of Confucians from corvée—all of which Wenzong approved.

sentences.zh: 顥先後居集賢，署薦士牘累數百，有訐之者，顥曰：「吾寧以謬舉受罰，蔽賢誠所不忍。
