translations.literal: Hao, while successively at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, signed recommendation documents for scholars numbering several hundred; when someone denounced this, Hao said: "I would rather be punished for mistaken recommendation than conceal talent, which I truly cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Academy, Hao signed hundreds of recommendation documents for scholars. When criticized, he said, "I would rather be punished for a bad recommendation than hide talent—that I cannot bring myself to do.

sentences.zh: 」順帝元統初，顥扈蹕行幸上都，至龍虎台，帝命造膝前，而握其手曰：「卿累朝老臣，更事多矣，凡議政事，宜極言無隱。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Yuantong of Shundi, Hao accompanied the imperial progress to Shangdu; arriving at Longhutai, the Emperor ordered him to come before his knee and, grasping his hand, said: "You are an old minister of many reigns and have seen much; whenever affairs of government are deliberated, you should speak to the utmost without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: " At the start of Shundi's Yuantong reign, Hao accompanied the court to Shangdu. At Longhutai the Emperor summoned him, took his hand, and said, "You have served many reigns and seen much; in all deliberations speak plainly and hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 」顥頓首謝不敏。

translations.literal: " Hao kowtowed and thanked him for his lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao kowtowed and humbly demurred.

sentences.zh: 顥每集議，其言無不剴切，後至元四年，致政，命食全俸於家。

translations.literal: Whenever Hao joined deliberations, his words were all incisive; later in the fourth year of Houzhiyuan he retired from office and was ordered to receive full salary at home.
translations.idiomatic: In every deliberation Hao spoke with sharp clarity. In the fourth year of Houzhiyuan he retired and was granted full salary at home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 至正十四年，贈攄誠秉義佐理功臣、光祿大夫、河南江北等處行中書省平章政事、柱國，追封薊國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng, he was posthumously granted Merit Lord Who Displays Sincerity, Upholds Righteousness, and Assists in Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor of the Henan and Jiang-Bei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, with the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted Merit Lord Who Displays Sincerity, Upholds Righteousness, and Assists in Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, grand councillor of the Henan and Jiang-Bei Branch Secretariat, and Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 顥出入禁闥數十年，樂談人善，而惡聞人過。

translations.literal: Hao entered and left the forbidden gates for several decades, delighted to speak of others' good points and loathing to hear of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: For decades Hao moved in and out of the inner court, delighting in praising others' virtues and refusing to hear their faults.

sentences.zh: 大夫士因其薦拔以至顯列，有終身莫知所自者，是以結知人主，上下無有怨尤。

translations.literal: Great officials and gentlemen because of his recommendation and promotion reached conspicuous rank; some never knew in their whole lives from whom it came; therefore he bound himself to knowing the sovereign, and above and below there was no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials he recommended rose to high rank, some never knowing who had helped them; thus he won the trust of the throne, and neither court nor subjects bore him resentment.

sentences.zh: 歐陽玄為國子祭酒，與顥同考試國子伴讀，每出一卷，顥必拾而觀之，苟得其片言善，即以置選列，為之色喜。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xuan was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; with Hao he jointly examined the companion readers of the Directorate; whenever a paper was produced, Hao would pick it up and read it; if he obtained even a good phrase he would place the candidate in the selected rank and show pleasure in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xuan was chancellor of the Directorate of Education, he and Hao jointly examined student readers. Hao would read every paper; if he found even one good phrase he would advance the candidate and brighten with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 玄歎曰：「陳公之心，蓋篤於仁而逾於厚者，真可使鄙夫寬、薄夫敦矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan sighed and said: "Master Chen's heart is surely one that is earnest in benevolence and exceeds in generosity—truly able to make the petty broad and the cold-hearted warm."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan sighed and said, "Master Chen's heart is steeped in benevolence and overflowing with generosity—it could truly broaden the narrow-minded and warm the cold-hearted."

sentences.zh: 次子敬伯，至正中仕為中書參知政事，歷左丞、右丞，二十七年，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: His second son Jingbo, in the Zhizheng period served as Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat, served as Left Chancellor and Right Chancellor, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jingbo served in the Zhizheng period as associate administrator of the Central Secretariat, then as left and right chancellor, and in the twenty-seventh year was appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.
